introduction: Today we celebrate the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary. At the end of her earthly life, Mary was taken up body and soul into the glory of heaven. The Book of Revelation shows a woman clothed with the sun; Paul tells us that in Christ all will be made alive. In the Gospel, Mary visits Elizabeth and sings her Magnificat. Let us rejoice with Mary and ask her to lead us to her Son.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God has done great things for Mary, and he lifts up the lowly. With her, let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that, following Mary, she may believe God's word and proclaim his greatness. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the humble and the poor: that God may lift them up and fill the hungry with good things. Let us pray to the Lord.
For mothers and for all women who suffer: that Mary may watch over them and comfort them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our loved ones who have died: that they may share in the Resurrection of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may keep our eyes on heaven, where Mary has gone before us. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Almighty God, you took the Virgin Mary, mother of your Son, body and soul into heavenly glory. Keep our hearts set on heaven, and bring us to share in her glory. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Great things for me
reflection.body:
In 1950 Pope Pius XII solemnly defined what the Church had long believed: that Mary, at the end of her earthly life, was taken up body and soul into heavenly glory. Today's feast is about Mary, but it is also about us. What God has done for her, he promises to all who belong to Christ.

Paul explains: "For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive." Christ is "the first fruits," and "then those who are Christ's at his coming." Mary, who belonged entirely to Christ, already shares fully in his victory over death. "The last enemy that will be abolished is death."

The Book of Revelation shows "a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars." The Church has long seen in this woman both Mary and the Church herself, threatened by the dragon but protected by God.

In the Gospel, Mary visits her cousin Elizabeth, who greets her: "Blessed is she who believed, for there will be a fulfillment of the things which have been spoken to her from the Lord!" Mary answers with a song of praise: "My soul magnifies the Lord." She sings of a God who "has put down princes from their thrones, and has exalted the lowly. He has filled the hungry with good things."

Mary is lifted up because she was lowly; she is glorified because she believed. Her Assumption is the Magnificat fulfilled.

Today, pray the Magnificat slowly, perhaps at evening. Thank God for the great things he has done for you. And let Mary's glory remind you of where your own life is heading: not to the grave, but to the glory of God.
